squid is streamlined for speeding backward faster than a fish of the same size can swim forward. The squid

has jetpropulsion by drawing water in through the wide mantle opening and then sending it out through a funnel by contracting the bands of muscles around its body. Curiously the

jet system is basically the respiratory gill system that all mollusks have. It

has one heart for the body and one heart for each gill, giving each gill effectively a supercharger. To stay at

the proper levels far above the ocean floor it has a depth organ made of sacs with weights in them to tell whether they are going up or down.

A parallel could be made between the squid and an airplane, rocketshaped, jetpropelled, supercharged, and with an altimeter.
